stem.en:
In a made-up stack of undisturbed rock, layer A lies below layer B. Layer A holds a broad leaf fossil, and layer B holds a divided frond fossil.

Which conclusion does this evidence support?

text.en: The fossil that scientists found first must be the older of the two.

feedback.en: The date of a find is about people. The age of a fossil follows from its layer.

text.en: A’s fossil is older, so its plant must be the direct ancestor of B’s plant.

feedback.en: Order in rock shows age only. Two plants can live at different times with neither being the ancestor of the other.

text.en: A’s fossil is older, but that does not make it the ancestor of B’s.

feedback.en: Right. The order of undisturbed layers shows which is older, and it stops there.

text.en: B’s frond proves that every living thing becomes more complex with time.

feedback.en: Two fossils cannot show a rule for all living things, and the pattern in layers holds only generally.

explanation.en: In undisturbed rock, a lower layer is older. That gives the order of the two fossils, but not a family link between them.

hints.en: Separate when a layer formed from when someone found its fossil.
Being older is not the same as being an ancestor.

flags: L10 s04 is the outlined worked layer comparison rendered as one evidence-based MCQ, preserving eight slides. The single-beat scene shows the complete supplied evidence and candidate inference arrows neutrally; it must not reveal the answer before submission or rely on a question feedback hook. All scientific resolution is in option feedback/explanation. The fossil silhouettes are original, not a purple-frog ancestry claim or reproductions of Birbal Sahni specimens.
